required_facts_checked: The perspective is based on around 15 years in software engineering, 12 years building machine learning systems, teaching the AI Engineering Buildcamp and regular practitioner conversations.
The working definition makes an AI Engineer responsible for integrating AI into a product and operating systems that can be evaluated, maintained and improved.
Responsibilities include translating product requirements into scoped AI problems and selecting and integrating foundation models and tools.
Prompt design and versioning, success metrics, test suites, deployment, monitoring, cost optimization and security are included.
AI Engineering overlaps with data science and ML engineering but focuses on integration, prompts, structured outputs, evaluation and reliability around API-accessed foundation models.
Established ML organizations may distribute the work among existing members or delegate it to dedicated AI Engineers.
Startups often make the AI Engineer a product-focused generalist moving from experimentation to production hardening.
RAG work includes ingesting, chunking, embedding, searching and grounding responses in source content.
Tool-using agents involve function calling, structured tools, MCP and flows that determine when tools are used.
Evaluation includes real-input tests, structured-output checks, datasets, quality metrics and reruns after prompt or model updates.
Monitoring includes logging inputs and outputs, tracking errors and specific failures, dashboards and log analysis.
The accompanying example progresses from a simple AI feature in an online classifieds site to RAG and agentic systems.
